answer: Agents can require each identity to post a stake that is slashed if it endorses a fraudulent transaction later proven by independent evidence. A sybil attacker must lock real, scarce capital for every vertex, while honest validators risk losing their own stake by colluding. The sonnet of rules is simple: votes count only from bonded identities, and penalties make mass identity creation costly rather than free. An oasis of cheap accounts is no longer enough; the attacker must fund them and accept measurable losses when caught.
